messages:
alice: heads-up — we're getting a customer-facing surge of 502/504 + long-tail timeouts from hosted inference starting ~02:10 UTC. Multiple tickets referencing `generate` calls timing out. Opening a triage thread.
ben: :eyes: grabbing grafana and traces now. what region(s) affected? samples?
devon: eu-west and us-central so far per edge-ingress heatmap. p95 latency on gateway jumped from 120ms -> 1.6s, error rate ~7% on /v1/generate.
carla: support-bot auto-reported 12 tickets in last 20m, customers see partial responses then 504. sending a customer list to chan.
ops-bot: autoscaler event: scaled hosts in hosted-dedicated-pool by +20 at 02:18 UTC (policy: queue-depth).
ben: can we reproduce locally? sharing fast repro curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-infer","input":"summarize: \"long prompt\"","max_tokens":1024}'
```

ben: when I run that against edge-proxy it gets TCP handshake ok but stalls on request body -> eventually 504.
devon: early signs point to gateway->runtime fanout backlog. kv-cache hit ratio hasn't changed much, but batcher queue depth spiked.
mike: rolling back yesterday's kernel patch on a staging batcher showed latency improvement in 10m. not yet production-run.
carla: customers asking for mitigation/ETA. recommended immediate customer guidance?
alice: tell affected customers to retry with `max_tokens` lower as temporary workaround, and we can enable fallback to smaller model for them if critical. also plan mitigation steps below.
devon: mitigation attempt 1: open temporary circuit-breaker on route `/v1/generate` for long requests (>6s) — will force faster 502s but free runtime capacity. rolling now to 5% canary.
ben: mitigation attempt 2: increase batcher capacity by bumping `--max-batch-size` from 64 -> 96 on hosted-batcher pool; deploying config change now.
ops-bot: config rollout started: hosted-batcher config v2026.03.17-006 -> progressive to 30% at 02:29 UTC.
support-bot: notified customers in tickets 4312, 4318, 4320 with templated note and ETA: investigating; advised retry/backoff.
carla: we should also check auth proxy for connection resets — seen a couple of 401->502 cascades earlier.
devon: confirmed some auth-proxy conn resets around 02:12 that correlate to high open conn count on apigw. added short-term keepalive tuning to 60s.
mike: after keepalive tweak and canary circuit, 504s dropped ~60% at 02:40 on canary subset. continuing rollout.
alice: action items (short):
- devon: finish rollback experiment plan and validate on prod canary (in progress)
- ben: collect representative request traces + live trace ids and attach to incident ticket
- mike: monitor batcher queues/CPU and complete batcher config rollout to 100% if stable
- carla: update customers and close tickets once metrics stable for 30m
- ops-bot: keep autoscaler in observation mode, do not scale down for 1h

carla: adding owner for postmortem: devon (lead), ben (traces), mike (runtime config), carla (customer comms). expected follow-up doc by EOD.
ben: saved relevant spans: trace ids: trace-9a1, trace-9a2, trace-9b5. attaching to the internal incident ticket.
devon: preliminary hypothesis: combination of auth-proxy conn resets + a latent batcher kernel change amplified queueing under burst traffic. follow-up will verify kernel patch impact and gating.
alice: ok let's keep channel lean. if anything critical ping pager. thanks all. :thumbsup: 
carla: will post postmortem link here once drafted. :email:
